evidence: The Anglo-Dutch Wars (11), Marlborough (2), and the malformed Liberty Secured? entry (1) are J. R. Jones's: about 14/23 listed citation weights. The Thin Red Line, From Here to Eternity and La Ligne rouge are the novelist's; Creating Revolution is James Thomas Jones III's. Mixed majority, below the brief's approximate two-thirds threshold; conservative borderline verdict.

The governance books and articles are R. A. W. Rhodes's, accounting for 22/24 listed citation weights. The Sanctuary of Artemis Brauronia on the Athenian Akropolis (2) is explicitly signed Robin F. Rhodes and John J. Dobbins.

Patron-Client Politics is explicitly James C. Scott's, as are the peasant-resistance and Moral Economy titles. The Settlement of Huron County is James Richardson Scott's; the Monmouth declaration is another James Scott's. None of the listed titles is identifiable as a work of international lawyer James Brown Scott.

other_people: Kenneth Wolf (author of the 1972 Hans Kohn dissertation)
evidence: The Pomona key is Kenneth Baxter Wolf: Moors (6), Conquerors and Chroniclers (4), Making History (3), Poverty of Riches (2), and the Spain/Islam/chronicle/crusade pieces give about 20/25 citation weights. Medieval Scandinavia and Color Grey are Kirsten Wolf's; Ioannes Malalas (1916) is Karl Wolf's, and the 1972 Kohn dissertation predates Baxter Wolf's scholarly career.

Crofters and Habitants (12), Nationalism, Capitalism, and Colonization (10), Patrician Liberal (5), and the three Eastern Townships articles (6) are John Irvine (Jack/J. I.) Little's: 33/34 citation weights. The sole outlier, Between Cultures: Sioux Warriors and the Vietnam War, is John A. Little's 2014 master's thesis; nearly all weight belongs to the key.

Stevedores and Dockers (7), British Trade Unions (2), and A Short History of the TUC (1) are John Christopher Lovell's: 10/20 listed citation weights. Neither Athens Nor Sparta and the military-policy works belong to John Philip Lovell; Black Song is John Lovell Jr.'s; several Montreal entries are publisher contamination. An approximately even split supports neither a clear two-thirds majority nor a strict minority.

History/New History of Orkney, Funzie, Fetlar, Little General, and the Orkney farming/kelp/linen chapters are William P. L. Thomson's: about 14/19 citation weights. Lincolnshire Assize Roll is Walter Sinclair Thomson's, History of Tapestry is William George Thomson's, History of Manchester is W. H. Thomson's, and the early travel books are other authors' works.

Farewell to the Party of Lincoln (9), National Urban League (6), the two Negro and New Freedom entries (2), and Charles Francis Murphy (1) are Nancy Joan Weiss, later Malkiel: 18/22 citation weights. Mother, the Invention of Necessity (3) and Mother-Child Dyad Revisited (1) are Nancy Pottishman Weiss's.

Kwok-bun Chan's Montreal/refugee/business works total 10/20 positive citation weights. Abrogation of British Extraterritoriality (5) and Reorganization Loan (1) are K. C. Chan's. The three ecosystem-services records are Kai M. A. Chan's; the Hui/Chan Habitat International record is another Chan's. Approximately half belongs to the key, so neither a two-thirds majority nor a strict minority is established.

David William Foster wrote Culture and Customs of Argentina, Mexico City in Contemporary Mexican Cinema, Homoerotic Diaspora, and the 1990 review of Las Canciones del Inmigrante: about 4/16 citation weights. Forests in Time, Thoreau's Country and the forest-history papers are ecologist David R. Foster's; the South African books are Don Foster's, the evacuation article Diane Foster's, and NIMBY another David Foster's.
